UI/UX Audit — 5 platforms + cross-platform experience

The Greyin Ecosystem, Reviewed

Every platform audited against the criteria a social or marketplace product gets graded on — onboarding friction, navigation, empty states, accessibility, mobile behavior — plus how well the five actually work as one ecosystem rather than five separate apps.

Scope Greyin B2B, GreyMatters, FreeAgent, Salt & Pepper, Prolab Reviewed against production Method rendered screenshots, desktop + mobile, plus source review

Scorecard

Individual platforms average 5.8/10. The cross-platform layer — the thing that's supposed to make five apps feel like one — scores lower than any single app.

Prolabverified work & track record 7.0/10 Greyin B2Brecruitment 6.5/10 Salt & Peppersenior community 6.0/10 FreeAgentfreelance marketplace 5.0/10 GreyMattersblog 4.5/10 Cross-platform experienceSSO, linking, consistency 5.0/10
Prolab prolab.greyin.net
7.0 / 10

Builders post real project asks; Supporters do the work and earn a verified, scored record. The newest product in the ecosystem, and it shows — most refined page-level design of the five.

Working well

  • Hero speaks to both audiences by name with two distinct CTAs, rather than one generic "Get Started" — a Builder and a Supporter each see themselves immediately.
  • The People directory and visible Greyin Score are a genuine first-impression trust feature none of the sibling apps have.
  • Signup's track picker ("Post a project" vs "Help build one") sets expectations before a single field is filled in.

Fix next

  • Mobile header is broken — nav text overlaps and clips the wordmark. Worst mobile bug in the ecosystem, on the newest app.
  • Empty states ("No one here yet", "0 projects") offer no next step tailored to whether the visitor is a prospective Builder or Supporter.
  • The verification pipeline (AI score, human review, 14-day window) is real product depth that's invisible until a visitor is deep into an ask — worth a one-line callout on the homepage itself.
Evidence — mobile viewport (390px): nav links render on top of the "Prolab" logo, and the "Sign Up" button clips to "Sig Up" at the right edge. No md:hidden/hamburger pattern exists anywhere in the codebase for any of the five apps.
Greyin B2B greyin.net
6.5 / 10

The flagship recruitment product, and the ecosystem's front door — its homepage is the only one that actually cross-promotes the other four.

Working well

  • Richest homepage of the five: a 6-card feature grid, a real "Explore Our Ecosystem" section linking all four sibling apps, and a closing CTA banner — this is the one page in the ecosystem that sells the whole idea.
  • Jobs listing has a genuinely useful filter sidebar (employment type, experience level, work location).
  • Signup's "Hire Talent / Find Jobs" split is immediate and unambiguous.

Fix next

  • Homepage stat badges — "10,000+ Active Jobs," "50,000+ Candidates" — are hardcoded copy, not live counts. The jobs page one click away shows 0 jobs found. That gap is the first thing a skeptical visitor will notice.
  • Header nav differs between pages: the homepage shows "Find Talent" and a "More Platforms" dropdown; the jobs page swaps those for "Ecosystem Search" and drops the dropdown entirely. Same app, two different navigation menus.
Evidence — homepage nav: Browse Jobs · Companies · Find Talent · More Platforms ▾ · Sign In · Get Started. Jobs page nav: Browse Jobs · Companies · Ecosystem Search · Sign In · Get Started.
Salt & Pepper saltnpepper.greyin.net
6.0 / 10

An invite-flavored lounge for 12+-year professionals. The clearest, most specific positioning of any product here.

Working well

  • Category list has real personality — "War Stories," "Referrals & Intros," "Architecture Reviews" — instead of a generic "General" bucket.
  • Signup honestly says "Request an invite," not "Sign Up," matching the exclusivity the product is actually selling.
  • Hot / New / Top sort tabs on the discussion feed is a well-understood, low-friction pattern.

Fix next

  • Mobile header wraps the wordmark to two lines and the primary "Join Community" button is unreadable — the second-worst mobile break in the ecosystem, after Prolab.
  • "No discussions yet" is the only thing a first-time visitor to /discussions sees — no seeded content, no preview of what a good discussion looks like.
Evidence — mobile viewport: the "Salt & Pepper" wordmark line-wraps under its own icon, and Discussions · Members · Sign In compete for space with a "Join Community" button that has nowhere left to render.
FreeAgent freeagent.greyin.net
5.0 / 10

A 0%-commission gig marketplace. Has the most sophisticated listing-filter UI in the ecosystem, sitting behind the thinnest homepage.

Working well

  • "0% Platform Fee — keep 100% of your earnings" is a sharp, specific trust signal — more concrete than any other product's tagline here.
  • Gig filters (category, price band, delivery time, seller level) are the most complete faceted search of the five apps.
  • Gig cards now show a real seller rating or "New seller," and a Prolab verified-track-record badge when one exists — both added this session, replacing a hardcoded 4.9 (123) that shipped on every card regardless of actual reviews.

Fix next

  • Homepage is a hero and three stat cards, then nothing — no featured gigs, no category shortcuts, no ecosystem cross-link. Thinnest first impression of any product here.
  • The homepage nav has no "Join Now"/signup button at all — it only appears once a visitor clicks through to an inner page. Every other app puts its primary CTA in the homepage header.
  • The "Seller Level" filter (Top Rated / Level 2 / Level 1 / New Seller) implies a tier system the product doesn't actually have yet — the filter promises more than checkout delivers.
Evidence — homepage header: Browse Gigs · Sign In — no signup CTA. Gigs page header: Browse Gigs · Become a Seller · Ecosystem Search · Sign In · Join Now.
GreyMatters greymatters.greyin.net
4.5 / 10

The ecosystem's blog. Simplest product surface of the five — which makes its gaps harder to excuse, not easier.

Working well

  • Clean, uncluttered post-list layout with a sensible sidebar (categories, about, newsletter signup).
  • An RSS feed link in the footer — the only product here offering one, and the right instinct for a content site.
  • Authorship has deliberately no experience gate, unlike Salt & Pepper/Prolab's Builder track — the right call for a blog that wants contributors, not gatekeeping.

Fix next

  • The homepage header has no Sign In or Sign Up link at all — just Home, Categories, About. A first-time visitor has no visible path to an account. Worst onboarding funnel of the five products.
  • No cross-platform promotion anywhere on public pages — the "Explore Our Ecosystem" section only exists behind login, on /profile.
  • Posts have no cover-image treatment on the list page despite the app supporting image uploads — every entry is text-only, no visual hierarchy between posts.
Evidence — homepage header, in full: Home · Categories · About. No account entry point. (Login/signup exist at /login and /signup — they're simply not linked from the homepage nav.)

Cross-platform experience

The premise of the ecosystem is one identity across five products. The infrastructure for that is real and well-built — the experience of it is mostly invisible until a visitor is already signed in somewhere.

SSO / authentication

The strongest technical result in the ecosystem. One login genuinely carries a session across all five domains with zero re-authentication — verified end-to-end, not just claimed.

But it's unexplained: nothing on any public page tells a first-time visitor this is how it works. The only place it's ever surfaced is the EcosystemWidget on /profile, which requires already being signed in to see.

8 / 10
Cross-linking

Inconsistent by app. Greyin B2B's homepage has a full 4-card "Explore Our Ecosystem" section. GreyMatters, FreeAgent, Salt & Pepper, and Prolab have none of that on their own public homepages — it only appears post-login, on the profile page.

A visitor who lands directly on FreeAgent or Prolab — the two most likely entry points from a shared link — has no way to discover the other four products exist.

4 / 10
Ecosystem Search

A real, working cross-app search (platform_search_index) — not a stub. But it indexes only 3 of 5 pillars: jobs, gigs, and blog posts. Salt & Pepper discussions and Prolab projects are entirely absent from results, even though the nav link is labeled "Ecosystem Search" everywhere it appears.

5 / 10
Trust signals across products

This session's own work — a Prolab verified outcome showing up on a FreeAgent gig card or a Greyin B2B job application, and a single Greyin Score blending all three. No comparable multi-product ecosystem in this space does this today.

Currently reachable only after signup, on /profile or in-context on a listing — it strengthens retention and cross-sell, but does nothing for a pre-signup visitor deciding whether to join at all.

7 / 10
Mobile navigation

Broken across all five apps, to varying degrees. None has a responsive collapse — no hamburger pattern exists anywhere in the codebase. Header nav either overflows and wraps (Salt & Pepper), or wraps and visibly overlaps the logo with clipped button text (Prolab). This is the single highest-leverage fix in this whole audit: one shared pattern, five broken headers.

2 / 10
Visual consistency

Stronger at the component level than the navigation level. Card radius, button shape, spacing rhythm, and form-field styling are consistent across all five apps — a shared Tailwind convention is clearly being followed. Each product keeps its own accent color, which reads as intentional brand differentiation rather than inconsistency.

7 / 10
Accessibility

11 <img> tags across the codebase ship with no alt attribute at all — not even an empty one for decorative images, which is the correct pattern used elsewhere (e.g. Prolab's image uploader). A screen reader announces these as unlabeled or falls back to the filename.

4 / 10

If you fix five things

Ranked by how many people it affects and how little it costs to fix.

  1. Cross-platform · every app

    Give every header a real mobile menu

    One shared collapse pattern (hamburger + slide-down) fixes the worst bug on all five apps at once — currently zero of them have any responsive nav behavior at all.

  2. GreyMatters

    Put Sign In / Sign Up back in the homepage header

    Right now there's no visible account entry point on the one page every new visitor lands on first.

  3. Cross-platform · Ecosystem Search

    Add Salt & Pepper and Prolab to the search index

    platform_search_index is real infrastructure two migrations away from actually covering the whole ecosystem it's named after.

  4. Cross-platform · every homepage

    Put the ecosystem cross-link on every public homepage, not just Greyin B2B's

    Copy the "Explore Our Ecosystem" section that already exists and works — it's currently gated behind login on four of five products.

  5. Greyin B2B

    Replace the hardcoded homepage stats or drop them

    "10,000+ Active Jobs" next to a live listing page reading zero is the fastest way to lose a skeptical visitor's trust.

Methodology. Rendered screenshots captured against production at 1440×900 (desktop) and 390×844 (mobile), plus direct review of each app's page source, database schema, and RLS policies for claims that aren't visible on screen (search index coverage, image alt attributes, mobile-menu code). Content in several products is sparse because this audit ran against live production data, not seeded fixtures — empty states are graded on their own merits, not treated as missing content.
